title: Aegis kernel event v2 (single cross-OS contract)
description: One JSON line per event. Produced by the kernel collectors (eBPF on Linux, ETW on Windows) and consumed by the unified Go agent; the legacy Guard and NodeTrace consumers remain for 4.2.1 compatibility. Brain: EventSchema PROCESS_CREATED/PROCESS_EXITED/CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED. Compatibility: v1 = lines without schema_version (only pid/event_type required); consumers MUST accept v1 and v2, v2 producers MUST include schema_version=2, event_id, agent_id, boot_id and seq when available. Details in docs/archive/EVENT_SCHEMA_V2.md.

schema_version.description: 1 = legacy (absent = 1), 2 = M1 with identity and sequence

event_id.description: UUID v4 per event, generated by the agent: idempotency/dedup key

agent_id.description: ID of the agent that observed the event

boot_id.description: Endpoint boot ID: distinguishes PID reuse across reboots, anchors seq

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number per (agent_id, boot_id): detects loss and duplicates

ts_ns.description: MONOTONIC timestamp in nanoseconds (bpf_ktime_get_ns on eBPF). Never wall-clock.

ts_wall_ns.description: Wall-clock Unix timestamp in nanoseconds (FileTime on ETW, clock_gettime on eBPF when available)

proc_start_ns.description: Monotonic process start time: with pid, distinguishes PID reuse

uid.description: Unix UID; 0 on Windows (SIDs are not mapped in the MVP)

session.description: Session/logon (e.g. Windows session, Linux tty) when available

integrity.description: Integrity/privilege level (e.g. System/High/Medium on Windows, euid/caps on Linux)

filename.description: Canonical executable path; '' when unresolvable (exit, protected processes)

provenance.description: Source: ebpf-full | ebpf-partial | etw | auditd | polling

drop_reason.description: Set ONLY on synthetic loss-accounting events (never on real events)
